neighbours.label: a cause phrase fronted before its main clause (that because of X, ...; due to Y, ...), against the same phrase after the main clause
fire: Many owners say that because of the noise they moved out.
Worse still, because of new rules, prices rose.
A problem is that, due to wear, the seal leaks.
To this day, because of its odd shape, the tower draws tourists.
One issue: because of its weight, the cart tips.
Some suggest that because of heavy rain, crops failed.
Experts note that, due to erosion, the cliff moved.
In the end, because of poor sales, the shop closed.
quiet: The owners moved out because of the noise.
